chain.label: Dispatch and ATC failures before and during the flight
chain.trigger: AIRMET for icing was not included in the Flight Release; TMC released the flight from ground hold saying 'he might do some holding when he gets up here'; EFC extended four times without a PIREP solicited

chain.label: Aircraft held ~33 minutes at 10,000 ft in freezing drizzle/rain conditions outside the Appendix C certification envelope
chain.trigger: the aircraft was operating in and out of clouds for most of the 33 minutes it was in the hold ... ROSELAWN conditions were far outside App C certification envelope

caused_by.evidence: flight released and repeatedly held airborne despite forecast icing along its route

chain.label: Crew failed to maintain required icing procedures (86% NP, continuous de-icing) during early holding legs
chain.trigger: propeller speed was reduced to 77% NP ... Airframe deicing system was deactivated at 1523:12, just before entering the holding pattern

caused_by.evidence: TAT recorded below +7 degrees C with visible moisture present throughout the hold

chain.label: Crew violated sterile cockpit discipline with prolonged non-essential conversation, ACARS distraction, and the Captain's absence from the cockpit
chain.trigger: loud radio music continues for the next 18 minutes ... Captain unfastened his seat belt and left the cockpit at 1549:07 ... absent from the cockpit for over 5 minutes

caused_by.evidence: cockpit atmosphere lacked vigilance while operating in an acknowledged icing environment

chain.label: Crew selected an unauthorized Flap 15 holding configuration not provided for in the AOM/FCOM
chain.trigger: F.O.: 'you want flaps fifteen?' ... DFDR data indicates that the flap handle was moved to select the Flap 15 configuration

caused_by.evidence: Captain: 'man this thing gets a high deck angle in these turns ... we're just wallowing in the air'

chain.label: Crew observed ice accretion and received AAS caution chimes but never acknowledged or acted on them
chain.trigger: 'I'm showing some ice now' ... no response ... 'we still got ice' ... not acknowledged by the Captain

caused_by.evidence: Captain engaged in extensive discussions with the Junior Female Flight Attendant during the caution chime
single tone caution chimes at 1533:56 and 1541:07 recorded no crew discussion

chain.label: Ice ridge accreted aft of the de-icing boots upstream of the ailerons; flap retraction during descent triggered flow separation and an unexpected aileron hinge moment reversal
chain.trigger: accretion of a ridge of ice aft of the de-icing boots, upstream of the ailerons ... which led to a sudden roll upset following an unexpected Aileron Hinge Moment Reversal when the crew retracted the flaps during the descent

caused_by.evidence: prolonged operation of Flight 4184 in a freezing drizzle environment, well beyond the aircraft's certification envelope
utilizing a 15 degree flap holding configuration ... resulting in a negative outer wing local AOA during the accretion phase
NP left at 77% and de-icing deactivated during part of the accretion phase

chain.label: Autopilot disconnected and the aircraft rapidly rolled to 77 degrees bank, then rolled through inverted attitude with a steep nose-down pitch
chain.trigger: the autopilot disconnected. The left aileron then deflected abruptly downwards. The aircraft rapidly rolled to the right to a maximum bank angle of 77 degrees

caused_by.evidence: aileron hinge moment reversal at autopilot disconnection produced the roll upset

chain.label: Crew applied uncoordinated, ineffective control inputs during the upset, without transferring or coordinating control
chain.trigger: the First Officer and the Captain were pulling on the control column at different times without coordination. The CVR records no attempt to either transfer the controls to the Captain, or to coordinate flight control inputs

caused_by.evidence: roll upset and rapid attitude changes surprised the crew, who did not discuss the aircraft's attitude or how to respond

chain.label: Aircraft entered a steep inverted, high-speed dive and struck the ground near Roselawn, Indiana
chain.trigger: pitch attitude reached a maximum of 73 degrees nose-down. The airspeed increased to 296 KIAS ... analysis of the wreckage, made difficult by the extensive fragmentation of the aircraft

caused_by.evidence: no coordinated recovery inputs arrested the roll and nose-down pitch before impact

chain.label: All occupants aboard were killed in the crash
chain.trigger: 64 passengers, 2 flight attendants, and the 2 pilots on board the aircraft ... extensive fragmentation of the aircraft
